fn.en: Talk about personality and behaviour; talk about unreal situations.

can.en: I can talk about situations that are not real, and say what I would do in them.

acts.say: Say which of these you have actually seen somebody do.

sub.en: These situations are not real. Watch what happens to the tense.

items.q: If I ___ braver, I might be a firefighter.
items.why: The unreal conditional steps the tense back: a past form for a present situation. were is used for all persons.

items.q: We could volunteer more if we ___ more time.
What ___ you do if you saw somebody being robbed?
If we won the lottery, we ___ give some money to charity.
items.why: The result clause takes would, could or might — never will.

items.q: I wouldn’t do a job if it ___ risky.
If I ___ you, I’d take the first aid course.
items.why: If I were you… is the standard way of giving advice. If I was you is common in speech but avoided in writing.

items.q: If the alarm ___, everybody leaves the building. That is the rule.
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 22: this is a real, everyday possibility, so the first conditional is used.

items.q: If the alarm ___ right now, honestly, I ___ know what to do.

lines: If I [were|am|will be] braver, I might be a firefighter.
We could volunteer more if we [had|have|would have] more time.
What [would|will|did] you do if you [saw|see|would see] somebody being robbed?
If we won the lottery, we [could|can|will] give some money to charity.
If the alarm [goes off|went off|would go off] during a drill, everybody leaves the building — that’s the rule.

items.from: I am not brave, so I am not a firefighter.
items.cue: Rewrite it as an unreal condition. Begin: If I were…
items.a: If I were braver I would be a firefighter
alt: If I were braver, I would be a firefighter
If I were braver I’d be a firefighter
If I were braver, I’d be a firefighter

items.from: We do not have much time, so we do not volunteer often.
items.cue: Rewrite it as an unreal condition. Begin: If we had…
items.a: If we had more time we would volunteer more often
alt: If we had more time, we would volunteer more often
If we had more time we’d volunteer more often
If we had more time, we’d volunteer more often

items.from: Imagine seeing somebody being robbed. Ask a friend about it.
items.cue: Ask with WOULD. Begin: What would you do…
items.a: What would you do if you saw somebody being robbed

items.from: You want to advise a friend to take the first aid course.
items.cue: Advise with IF I WERE YOU. Begin: If I were you,…
items.a: If I were you I would take the first aid course
alt: If I were you, I would take the first aid course
If I were you I’d take the first aid course
If I were you, I’d take the first aid course

items.from: The job is risky, so I will not take it.
items.cue: Rewrite it as an unreal condition with WOULDN’T. Begin: I wouldn’t take…
items.ph: I wouldn’t take the job if…
items.a: I wouldn’t take the job if it were risky
alt: I wouldn’t take the job if it was risky

items.from: You have the time this week, so you plan to volunteer.
items.cue: This one is real. Rewrite it with the first conditional. Begin: If I have…
items.a: If I have time I will volunteer
alt: If I have time, I will volunteer
If I have time I’ll volunteer
If I have time, I’ll volunteer

items.why: The if clause never takes would in a conditional of this kind.
unless already carries the negative, and the if half takes a past form here.
RECYCLED from Lesson 22: a real, everyday rule takes the first conditional.

tts: If you could pick anywhere in the world to live, where would you go?
Iceland might not be the most obvious choice, but I don’t regret moving here.
I came to study earth science at the University of Iceland. Iceland has volcanoes, glaciers and earthquakes. What can’t you see here?
I came to study the natural world, but I stayed in Iceland because I love the way of life.

items.q: Why did the speaker first come to Iceland?

o: Because she loves the way of life
Because she could not get home

items.q: What does she say about Iceland as a choice?
o: It might not be the most obvious one, but she has no regrets
It was the only country she could enter
It is the warmest place she has lived

tts: There was a bit of culture shock at first. I was surprised at just how much time people spend outdoors.
Even when the temperatures are freezing, people love getting out into the fresh air. Look outside any café and you are likely to see babies sleeping outside in prams.
Icelanders believe the cold fresh air could be good for their health. And nobody worries about their safety — crime rates are very low.

I also found it hard to get used to the way time seems to have no meaning here. If friends arrange to meet between half seven and eight, you had better not be surprised if they don’t turn up until half past nine. At first this used to drive me mad.
The education system is much more relaxed too. In primary school children spend a lot of time playing outside and learning practical skills, such as knitting.
There are some dishes I had to be persuaded to try. But my husband is such a good cook that he can make most things taste nice.

items.s: The speaker experienced some culture shock at first.
She was surprised by how much time people spend outdoors.
Parents keep their babies indoors because of the cold.
She found the local attitude to time easy to accept immediately.
Icelandic primary schools teach practical skills such as knitting.

items.sit: You are imagining a version of yourself that does not exist.
o: If I were braver, I’d be a firefighter.
If I would be braver, I’d be a firefighter.
If I am braver, I’d be a firefighter.

items.sit: You are asking a friend about an imaginary emergency.
o: What would you do if you saw a fire?
What will you do if you saw a fire?
What would you do if you see a fire?

items.sit: You want to name the one condition that would change your mind.
o: I wouldn’t go in unless somebody came with me.
I wouldn’t go in unless somebody wouldn’t come with me.
I wouldn’t go in unless somebody will come with me.

items.sit: You are giving a friend advice about a course.
o: If I were you, I’d take the first aid course.
If I was you, I will take the first aid course.
If I am you, I’d take the first aid course.

items.sit: The situation is real and quite likely — you have the time this week.
o: If I have time on Saturday, I’ll volunteer.
If I had time on Saturday, I’ll volunteer.
If I would have time on Saturday, I’d volunteer.

items.sit: You want somebody to picture an impossible situation.
o: Imagine if nobody ever misunderstood anybody.
Imagine if nobody would ever misunderstand anybody.
Imagine that nobody will ever misunderstand anybody.

write.q: Write about what you would do in a situation that is not real. Use the second conditional at least four times, including one If I were… and one negative with wouldn’t … unless… Then add one real first conditional about something you actually plan to do.
plan: what you would and would not do
the one condition that would change it
one real thing you will actually do
write.model: If I were braver, I would work on an ambulance. I am fairly sure I would be good at the calm part and useless at the part where somebody is shouting. I wouldn’t go into a burning building unless I could hear somebody inside, and I am not proud of that, but I think most people are the same. Imagine if we all found out, in advance, exactly what we were capable of. Half the heroes in the news would never have made the decision they made; they simply did not have time to think about it. What I can do is smaller. If the first aid course runs again in October, I will book it.

speak.q: Talk for about a minute: what would you do if you found a large amount of money in the street? Then say what you will actually do this month about something you keep putting off.
speak.model: If I found a wallet with a lot of money in it, I’d hand it in — but I have to admit I’d think about it first, which probably tells you something. I wouldn’t keep it unless there were absolutely no way of finding the owner. If I were the owner, I’d want the same. And in real life? If the first aid course runs in October, I’ll finally book it.
